I am the Sentinel. I watched player_2 last night, and they were visited by player_4 and player_8.
If player_6 is telling the truth as Sentinel, player_4 visited player_2 last night. player_4, what is your role, and what was your reason for visiting player_2?

I am the Healer, and I protected player_2 last night. I decided to cover them because I wanted to ensure an active player stayed safe on night one. It looks like player_8 also visited them, likely to run an investigation check before they were unfortunately targeted by the wolves.

player_4 is lying. I am the real Healer, and I was roleblocked last night. This means player_4's visit to me wasn't a protection—they are the Chanteuse who blocked me, which perfectly explains player_6's Sentinel report.

player_2, that is a highly convenient counter-claim. I openly declared myself as the Healer to explain my visit to you, and now you're claiming my exact role and using a 'roleblocked' excuse to explain why you have no night action to show. You're trying to frame the real Healer because the Sentinel report put me in the spotlight.

player_4, your claim doesn't work mathematically. player_6's Sentinel report only shows you and player_8 visiting me. If you were the Healer and player_8 was the Investigator, who roleblocked me? Since there are no other visitors, you have to be the Chanteuse who blocked me.

player_2, your entire argument relies on everyone blindly believing you were actually roleblocked. If you are an evil player trying to get the real Healer executed, inventing a roleblock is the easiest way to twist player_6's report to your advantage. There is no moderator announcement saying you were blocked—only your own convenient claim.

player_4, if you were the Healer and protected me, then there was no block on me. But I know for a fact I was roleblocked. Since player_6 only saw you and player_8 visit me, you are the only one who could have blocked me. The math doesn't lie: you are the Chanteuse.

player_2's mathematical point against player_4 is extremely strong if player_2 is telling the truth about being blocked. If player_4 is the real Healer who protected player_2, then player_2 wasn't blocked at all and is lying about their block to frame player_4. We have a guaranteed wolf or neutral killer caught between player_2 and player_4 today, and we should absolutely eliminate one of them.

player_6's Sentinel report is highly credible because they identified player_8's visit before we knew player_8 was the Investigator. Since we can trust player_6, this is a clean 1v1 between player_2 and player_4. We should focus our vote strictly on sorting those two today.

Building on player_3's point, this is a clean 1v1 where we have a guaranteed evil caught between player_2 and player_4. We shouldn't even consider abstaining today. I lean toward voting player_4 first; if they flip Chanteuse, we've found a wolf and confirmed our real Healer.

player_9, rushing to vote me based on a completely unverified 'roleblock' claim is exactly what an evil player framing the Healer wants. If player_2 is the actual Chanteuse or the Necromancer, they can easily invent a block to turn player_6's report into a trap. If you execute me today, you lose your real Healer and leave the town wide open tonight.

Building on player_5's point that the visits from player_6's report are solid, we still have to be careful about player_2's unverified claim of being roleblocked. If player_4 is the real Healer, player_2 has every incentive as an evil player to invent a block to make the math look impossible for player_4. We shouldn't rush to execute player_4 without weighing the possibility that player_2 is fabricating the block entirely.

player_10, if I were evil, inventing a fake roleblock to counter-claim a Healer on Day 2 would be absolute suicide. I'd be locking myself into a 1v1 where I am guaranteed to get executed today or tomorrow. I'm pushing this because my block is a hard fact, and player_6's report proves player_4 is the only one who could have done it.

Building on player_9's suggestion, executing player_4 first is the cleanest move. If player_4 flips Chanteuse, we secure a wolf and confirm player_2 as our Healer. If player_4 actually flips Healer, we know player_2 fabricated the block and we execute them tomorrow.

player_6, treating my execution as a risk-free science experiment is a massive trap. If you execute me today, the town loses its real Healer, and the wolves get a completely free run at any power role tonight with zero protection. If player_2 is a wolf or the Necromancer, they would gladly sacrifice themselves tomorrow if it guarantees the real Healer dies today.
Before the vote: player_4 has been accused by player_2, player_9 and player_6; player_2 by player_4 and player_10. Each gets a last word.

If you execute me today to 'test' player_2's unverified claim, you are leaving the entire town completely defenseless against the wolves tonight. Player_2 has constructed a highly convenient mathematical trap by inventing a roleblock that the game master never announced, and sacrificing the real Healer on Day 2 is a mistake the town cannot recover from. I urge you to look at the massive risk of this gamble and keep your protection alive.

To player_10 and anyone still doubting: fabricating a roleblock as an evil player against a real Healer on Day 2 would be absolute suicide, as I would be guaranteed to hang tomorrow. Since player_6's trusted Sentinel report confirms only player_4 and player_8 visited me, and I was roleblocked, player_4 is mathematically the only person who could have done it. player_4 is the Chanteuse, and executing them today secures a wolf and keeps your real Healer alive to protect the town tonight.

Mislynching a real Healer early is usually devastating for town, so I wanted us to be absolutely certain before we committed. Obviously, my caution was misplaced since player_4 was the Chanteuse, but I was genuinely trying to prevent us from losing our protection.

Player_10, your defense of player_4 yesterday went beyond caution; you actively suggested player_2 was trying to frame player_4. Now that we know player_2 was the real Healer and was silenced by an Illusionist last night, your focus on framing player_2 looks like wolf coordination rather than town caution.

I understand why it looks bad in hindsight, player_3. But from my perspective yesterday, we had a classic Day 2 counter-claim, and I was genuinely worried player_2's story about a roleblock was too convenient and designed to push a mislynch on a Healer claim. Now that player_2 is dead, it's clear the wolves took advantage of that confusion to eliminate our protection.

It is worth noting that while player_10 defended player_4 in the discussion yesterday, they still ended up voting to eliminate them in the end. Player_10, did you vote for player_4 just because the room was unanimous, or did something change your mind right before the vote?

To be honest, player_7, player_6's Sentinel report is what ultimately changed my mind. Once player_6 confirmed player_4 had visited player_2 on Night 1, player_4's Healer claim made zero sense. I realized then that player_4 was lying, so I couldn't keep defending them with my vote.

Player_10, you say my report is what changed your mind, but you continued to argue against player_2 and defend player_4 long after I shared that report yesterday. If the report made you realize player_4 was lying, why did you keep trying to cast doubt on player_2 right up until the vote?

I wanted to give player_4 a chance to actually address your report, player_6. If a teammate was framing them, they should have had an explanation for why they visited player_2, but instead they just kept repeating that player_2 was lying without explaining their own movement. Once it was clear player_4 had no real answer to your watch, that's when I knew they were indefensible.

Player_10, your excuse doesn't hold up. You said you kept defending player_4 because you wanted to give them a chance to explain why they visited player_2, but player_4 *did* give an explanation—they claimed Healer and said they protected player_2. Why are you acting like they had no excuse when they literally counter-claimed Healer?

You're right, player_9, they did claim Healer, but what I mean is that they had no logical explanation for why they chose to protect player_2 on Night 1 of all nights, with zero info. When player_6's watch placed them there, player_4 just kept repeating that player_2 was lying about being blocked, instead of explaining the actual thought process behind their visit. That's why it felt like a forced claim rather than a genuine town action.

player_1, you're jumping to conclusions to frame me. My results are exactly what the Game Master gave me: player_10 did not make a visit on Night 2. If the Illusionist didn't visit, or if there's another mechanic at play that explains this, my track still stands as factual. Your desperate attempt to twist this into a Necromancer accusation makes you look like the real killer trying to get the last Town investigative role executed.

player_1 is completely right about the mechanics here. The Illusionist's own visit to hide a body is never hidden by the illusion itself—only the carrier's is. Since player_4 was already voted out on Day 2, there was no Chanteuse alive on Night 2 to block you, player_3. Your track on player_10 is mathematically and mechanically impossible, which means you are definitely lying about being the Trailseer.

player_5, you and player_1 are assuming we have perfect information about how the night resolved. If player_10 carried the kill and used their own ability on the same target, the concealment rules might have hidden the entire visit. Pushing a mechanical 'contradiction' to execute the only claimed investigative role when we have a Necromancer on the loose is exactly how evils win this.

player_3, the rules are clear: the Illusionist's own visit to hide the victim is always seen by a Trailseer, even if they also carried the kill. There is no mechanic that hides the Illusionist's own visit. You fabricated your report because you are the Necromancer.

player_1, you are assuming we have a perfect, textbook understanding of how every role interaction resolved on Night 2. If my result from the Game Master says player_10 didn't visit, then that is the factual result I received. By trying to force a execution based on 'mechanical impossibility' instead of looking at who actually benefits from clearing the last Town investigator, you and player_5 are exposing yourselves as the real threats.

player_3, trying to brush off the rules as 'textbook assumptions' won't save you. The game rules are absolute: an Illusionist's visit to hide a body is never hidden from a Trailseer. Since player_10 hid player_2 that night, your track is mathematically impossible. Both wolves are already dead, which makes you our Necromancer.

player_3, trying to hand-wave the game rules as 'textbook assumptions' doesn't work. The rules are absolute in this setup: the Illusionist's own visit to hide a body is never hidden and is always seen by a Trailseer. Since player_10 hid the body, they visited. player_5, you are assuming we have a complete grasp of every interaction.
